status_summary: The government expanded DOE's role in reactor demonstration and deployment rather than limiting it. On 2025-12-02 DOE selected the Tennessee Valley Authority and Holtec for up to 400 million dollars each in cost-shared funding under its Gen III+ small modular reactor program to build first-mover plants, and Executive Order 14301 (signed 2025-05-23) directed DOE to create a Reactor Pilot Program, under which Nuclear News reported on 2026-07-02 that three privately developed reactors had reached DOE-authorized criticality; DOE's Nuclear Energy Launch Pad, reported 2026-03-09, extends the pilot programs. DOE announced conditional HALEU fuel allocations on 2025-08-26, including for a pilot program reactor, and the Office of Nuclear Energy continues under the Under Secretary for Energy after the 2025-11-20 reorganization. Congress's FY2026 appropriation (Public Law 119-74, 2026-01-23) provided 1.685 billion dollars for Nuclear Energy, above the 1.37 billion requested, and transferred 3.1 billion dollars of infrastructure law funds for up to two advanced small modular reactors, per CRS.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14301 signed, directing DOE to create a Reactor Pilot Program (published 2025-05-29).

DOE reorganization chart moved the Office of Nuclear Energy under the Under Secretary for Energy; the office remains.

DOE selected the Tennessee Valley Authority and Holtec for up to 400 million dollars each in federal cost-shared funding under the Gen III+ small modular reactor program to deploy first-mover reactor plants, from a 900 million dollar solicitation issued in March 2025.

FY2026 Energy and Water appropriations enacted (P.L. 119-74); per CRS, Nuclear Energy received 1.685 billion dollars and 3.1 billion dollars of infrastructure law funds were transferred for small modular reactor demonstrations.
DOE announced the Nuclear Energy Launch Pad extending and expanding the reactor and fuel line pilot programs.
Nuclear News reported three pilot program reactors had reached DOE-authorized criticality, meeting the 2026-07-04 goal.

title: Limit DOE Nuclear Energy scope and start no new reactor demonstrations
uncertainties: The pilot reactors are developed by private companies under DOE authorization, and Executive Order 14301 does not describe DOE funding for them; on their own they could be read as regulatory facilitation, so the diverged call rests mainly on the Gen III+ SMR awards and the larger budget. The DOE release does not name the funding appropriation or the office running the program, though the program page sits under the Office of Nuclear Energy's web path (an inference). The text respects existing contractual obligations; the SMR solicitation was issued in March 2025, after the period began. The ANS reorganization article is trade press. The FY2027 Nuclear Energy request was not checked.
